reason: The cited evidence (E1) only supports graphene's high strength and modulus, and its strengthening effect in Cu/graphene and Al/graphene composites via interface-mediated dislocation mechanisms. It provides no evidence for graphene's thermal conductivity, its ability to reduce interfacial thermal resistance, its bonding with tungsten, or its irradiation resistance. Thus, most key premises are unsupported.
premises: Graphene has exceptionally high intrinsic thermal conductivity
Graphene can form a coherent, well-bonded interlayer between tungsten and copper
The graphene interlayer reduces interfacial thermal resistance by facilitating electron and phonon transport
Graphene's strong bonding and 2D nature maintain mechanical integrity
Graphene can mitigate defect propagation under irradiation
